title: U.S. House · Arizona's 6th District
area: Southeastern Arizona: all of Cochise, Graham and Greenlee counties, plus part of Pima County including Tucson's eastern and southeastern suburbs (Sierra Vista, Sahuarita area).

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this race as a battleground. Ciscomani won re-election 50.7%-49.2% in 2022 and 50.0%-47.5% in 2024; Donald Trump carried the district 49.8%-49.1% in 2024. As of July 2026 election forecasters rated the general election Toss-up to Lean Democratic, and Ciscomani had raised $6.17 million to Mendoza's $7.35 million.

summary.text: Juan Ciscomani is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2022.

background.text: Born in Mexico; immigrated to Tucson, Arizona with his parents at age 5.
Graduated from Rincon High School in Tucson, earned an associate degree from Pima Community College, and a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona in 2005.

Worked as membership director and vice president of outreach for the Tucson Hispanic Chamber of Commerce, then as a senior advisor to Arizona Governor Doug Ducey (R) and vice chair of the Arizona-Mexico Commission.

priorities.text: Securing the border while making the legal immigration process faster and more workable, saying his own family's citizenship process took over a decade.
Reducing federal government spending, which he says has contributed to inflation in housing, groceries and other costs.
Addressing water conservation in Arizona through what he calls bipartisan effort.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (2025-2026), as vice chair of the Homeland Security Subcommittee and a member of the National Security, Department of State and Related Programs Subcommittee.
Serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (2025-2026), on the Economic Opportunity and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees.

candidates.name: JoAnna Mendoza

summary.text: JoAnna Mendoza, a retired U.S. Marine and Navy veteran, is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Juan Ciscomani.

background.text: Born in Florence, Arizona. Served in the U.S. Navy from 1994 to 1997 and the U.S. Marine Corps from 1998 to 2016, including two tours in Iraq and one in Afghanistan.
Earned a bachelor's degree from American Military University in 2013 and a master's degree from Grand Canyon University in 2019.
Worked as a veterans outreach coordinator for Pima Community College, a program manager at A Place Called Home, and a veteran services representative for U.S. Rep. Tom O'Halleran (D).
Ran unsuccessfully for the Arizona Senate in 2020.

priorities.text: Says she is committed to improving public education, increasing access to affordable healthcare, and preserving Arizona's natural environment and water resources.
Says she wants to ensure veterans, service members and their families get needed support.
Describes a focus on community access and engagement, working across the aisle, and action-oriented, implementable solutions.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to increasing access to affordable healthcare.
positions.quote: I am committed to improving our public education system, increasing access to affordable healthcare, and preserving our natural environment and scarce water resources.

candidates.researchNotes: Her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers on file (cited above) were submitted in 2020 for a state Senate race, not this 2026 congressional race; content is used only where it reflects durable personal background and stated values, not district-specific positions.

candidates.name: Gary Swing
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Green Party primary as a write-in candidate.

summary.text: Gary Swing is the Green Party candidate on the general-election ballot for Arizona's 6th Congressional District, a longtime perennial alternative-party candidate in Colorado and Arizona.

background.text: Born in Willingboro, New Jersey; earned a bachelor's degree (1991) and a master's degree (1999) in political science from the University of Colorado.

Career experience includes work as a cultural events promoter, a U.S. postal carrier, a produce receiver for Whole Foods, and a public policy research assistant at the University of Colorado Denver's Graduate School of Public Affairs.

Has run for office as an alternative-party candidate (mostly Green Party, also Unity Party of Colorado and others) at least a dozen times since 1996, in both Colorado and Arizona, including a 1996 U.S. Senate run in Arizona.
Former co-chair of the Colorado Coalition for Fair and Open Elections and former spokesperson for the election-reform group Best Democracy.

priorities.text: Says the U.S. should cut the military budget by 90%, close foreign bases, end foreign military aid and intervention, and abolish nuclear weapons.
Wants to replace the current system of government with a unicameral Congress elected by proportional representation and a parliamentary system, abolishing the U.S. Senate and Electoral College.
Supports Medicare for all, a universal basic income, and a 'steady state' economy built around environmental sustainability, including transition away from fossil fuels and nuclear energy.

positions.summary: Opposes continued U.S. military aid to Israel and says Israel has committed genocide against Gaza; supports war crimes tribunals and reparations.
positions.quote: Israel has committed genocide against Gaza. I support war crimes tribunals, reparations to the people of Gaza, and nonviolent conflict resolution.

positions.summary: Supports federal legislation to secure abortion rights.
positions.quote: Pass federal legislation to secure abortion rights.

positions.summary: Supports a single-payer healthcare system covering everyone.
Opposes immigration enforcement expansion; wants to abolish ICE, oppose a border wall, and allow freedom of migration.
positions.quote: Abolish ICE. Support "fair trade" policies and freedom of migration. No border wall.

positions.summary: Supports transitioning away from fossil fuels and nuclear energy to renewable energy sources as part of a sustainable, steady-state economy.
positions.quote: Transition away from fossil fuels and nuclear energy to renewable energy sources. Protect public lands.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no campaign finance activity or additional news coverage of this 2026 race found.

candidates.name: Jereme Peters

summary.text: Jereme Peters is the Libertarian Party candidate on the general-election ballot for Arizona's 6th Congressional District.

candidates.researchNotes: Checked https://ballotpedia.org/Jereme_Peters (September 2026): no biography, and Peters has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website or news coverage found beyond his listing as a candidate and FEC filer ($10,500 raised).

candidates.name: Michael Dorland

summary.text: Michael Dorland is an independent write-in candidate on the general-election ballot for Arizona's 6th Congressional District who has worked in information technology.

background.text: Grew up in rural South Dakota; his family lost their house and business when he was young, and he was briefly homeless as an adult.

Work history includes dishwasher and kitchen manager, retail jobs at K-Mart and Walmart, a Dell field service technician in southern Arizona, and owner of a comic store and other small businesses; his career has been in information technology.
Lost his house in 2008, largely due to medical debt, while raising two young children.

priorities.text: Says he is self-funded, taking no campaign donations and posting every expenditure publicly.
Wants stronger anti-corruption rules in Congress, including banning congressional stock trading and closing the revolving door to lobbying.
Calls for transparency on the water and power costs of AI data centers and safety testing of AI systems before they scale.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey with an extensive biography and platform, but his answers do not directly address any of the 15 tracked issue statements (his immigration views are described as being on his campaign website, which was not independently fetched). No FEC financial activity reported as of this filing period.
